messages:
Priya Shah: Heads up — FinRegCo legal just pushed back on the POC SOW. They want an explicit SLA penalty + hard data residency guarantees for EU only. Need answers this afternoon on routing behavior, subprocessor visibility, and what happens on failover. POC starts next week. @Marcus can you advise on feasible options and pricing impact?
Marcus Li: Short answer: we can do EU-only residency. Two modes: strict residency (reject outside-EU) or soft-pref (prefer EU, fallback to other region). If they require a hard guarantee, use strict residency + Dedicated capacity.
Priya Shah: If strict residency is enabled and EU pool is saturated, are requests queued or rejected? Customer wants a clause if >0.1% requests fail they'll levy penalties.
Lina Gomez: With strict_residency=true and hosted (no dedicated), requests are rejected (fast fail) when there is no capacity. For production SLAs with penalty exposure you should recommend Dedicated/reserved capacity to avoid rejects.
Sam Carter: Ballpark pricing for a small Dedicated POC (2x A10G equiv) in EU: ~$8k/mo. Add ~+20% for EU-only SLA + enhanced audit retention. If they want contractual SLA penalties, Legal requires capped liability in the MSA — that affects deal structure.
Oskar Petrov: For the security questionnaire: we can provide the subprocessors list (updated monthly), IP ranges, and audit log retention details. Hosted offers cloud KMS with EU key residency options; Private/on-prem supports customer-managed KMS/HSM.
Priya Shah: Legal asked for a minimal routing policy snippet they can put in the SOW. Can someone paste a simple example config we support?
Marcus Li: Sure — minimal policy we can sign off on:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  prefer_region: eu-west-1
  strict_residency: true   # rejects traffic that would leave EU
  fallback: none           # no cross-region fallback allowed
  reserved_capacity: true  # expect Dedicated pool for POC
  telemetry: audit-logs,region-tags
```
Priya Shah: Perfect. Also need the subprocessor CSV + list of EU region datacenter locations for their vendor security team. @Oskar can you send?
Oskar Petrov: Yep — I'll DM the full CSV and a short doc with region+location mapping. For quick reference, public regions page: https://redwood.com/docs/regions (shareable).
Priya Shah: One last practical Q from FinRegCo: they may want to start on Hosted with reserved quotas and move to Dedicated mid-POC. Is migration smooth or are there model/pinning blockers?
Marcus Li: No major blockers. We support model version pinning and canary rollouts. Moving to Dedicated requires flipping the `reserved_capacity` flag and provisioning the pool; KV cache state will be handled by infra. Expect a short window for capacity warm-up.
Priya Shah: Awesome, thank you everyone — I'll assemble a one-pager for Legal and the customer's infra team. If anyone has a short bullet list of risks/caveats for the SOW, drop them here. :thumbsup:
